note: Someone who plays with it all the time. The heavy end, about 1 home in 11 in Bentley's sample.
label: an enthusiast

moments_per_day.source: Bentley et al. 2018, IMWUT 2(3) Art. 91, Table 6, super-user cluster (8 of 88 homes): 5.93 sessions/day, 30.44 commands/day
moments_per_day.note: Picking the super-user cluster is part of the scenario. Company claims of 60+ interactions a day (bibo, ThePaper Oct 2026) are active-user counts and are not used

weekend.source: Bentley et al. 2018, IMWUT 2(3) Art. 91, Table 6: super users gave 30% of use on weekends

novelty.peak.source: Cagiltay et al. 2022 (IDC), Misty II, 14 homes
novelty.peak.note: Only measured magnitude: weekly use fell about 2.2x from week 1 to week 4 (Table 1, converting 'once a week'=1, 'a few times'=3, 'daily'=7). The conversion is an interpretation and the robot was a children's reading tutor, so the range is kept wide and swept

novelty.days.source: Weiss et al. 2021 (RO-MAN, Anki Vector): attachment dropped after 2 weeks · Bajones et al. 2019: novelty passed by 3 weeks · Cagiltay et al. 2022: still declining in week 4

long_term.floor.source: Kertész & Turunen 2017 (ICSR): long-term AIBO owners kept their robots for years (20% over 10 years) but usage frequency was not measured
long_term.floor.note: Range assumes heavy users stay at least half as engaged. Swept

long_term.from_day.source: Zhao & McEwen 2025: 'sharp drop after the first year' (recall)

long_term.to_day.source: Zhao & McEwen 2025: low and stable 'by years 3 to 4' (recall)

mix.source: Defines this household. No study measures how often people wave at, praise or insult a companion robot
mix.note: Results are conditional: 'in a home where moments look like this'. Only the proportions matter. Replace with real playtest proportions after week 10
